hook.text: Doctors once believed stomach ulcers came from stress. In 1982 Barry Marshall proved a bacterium caused them.

buildup.text: The medical community resisted for a decade. Their old model was comfortable and deeply embedded in practice.

discovery.text: Updating a model is harder than learning one. You must unlearn before you can relearn.

twist.text: Marshall drank the bacterium himself to prove his point. He got sick, then cured himself with antibiotics.

climax.text: He won the Nobel Prize. The lesson: treat every model as a draft, never a final copy.

punchline.text: Models are drafts, not dogma. Update often.

quiz.question: Why did the medical community resist the ulcer-bacteria discovery?
options: Their existing stress model was comfortable and deeply embedded
